Chapter 8: Islands—Laboratories of Evolution and Loss
Islands have always held a certain magic, haven’t they? Set apart by miles of open water, they turn into nature’s own laboratories—places where evolution can run wild, and the most unexpected creatures take shape.
But while islands can inspire with their unique life, they’re also incredibly fragile. Imagine a park ranger starting her morning on one of these remote islands, walking quiet trails and listening for birdsong that used to fill the air. Now, many of those voices are gone—silenced by rats, cats, or diseases that humans brought, sometimes without even realizing it.
Think about the dodo, the moa, the tiny Stephens Island wren... all gone in what feels like the blink of an eye, evolutionarily speaking.
Sadly, this story isn’t rare. Whenever people arrive on an island, they often bring more than just their backpacks and dreams. New animals, plants, and even microbes tag along—some intentionally, others by accident. And the local species, having evolved in isolation, just aren’t ready for these newcomers. With nowhere to escape, extinction can come swiftly, leaving behind only scattered bones and fading stories.
Yet, there’s a spark of hope. Islands have shown us that it’s possible to reverse some of the damage. Conservationists have worked for years in patient, painstaking ways—removing invasive species and giving native animals a fighting chance to return. It’s tough work, sometimes taking decades, but the results? They’re proof of what’s possible when people come together and decide to make a difference.
So, what do islands teach us? They remind us that isolation brings both wonder and fragility. The forces behind Earth’s sixth extinction aren’t just distant problems; they play out on every island, every isolated patch of nature. And the choices each of us makes—no matter how small they seem—can decide the fate of entire worlds.
